teaser.en: A roadside weed with a long green whip of a flower spike, dotted each morning with a few small blue flowers.
teaser.sw: Gugu la kando ya barabara lenye shada refu la kijani la ua kama mjeledi, linalopambwa kila asubuhi na maua machache madogo ya buluu.

summary.en: Mruwa is the blue porterweed, a low shrubby weed of open ground with small blue flowers on long, stiff spikes. Pakia lists it among the few plants the Digo identify by their flowers, because it is valued as an ornament.
summary.sw: Mruwa ni *blue porterweed*, gugu fupi lenye umbo la kichaka la maeneo ya wazi, lenye maua madogo ya buluu kwenye mashada marefu yaliyo magumu. Pakia anauorodhesha miongoni mwa mimea michache ambayo Wadigo huitambua kwa maua yake, kwa sababu unathaminiwa kama pambo.

about.en: Mruwa is a low, branching, somewhat woody herb, usually knee- to waist-high, with toothed, slightly rough leaves in opposite pairs. Its flowers come on long, thin green spikes that stand up like whips. Only a few flowers open at a time, small and bright blue to violet, set into the spike, and they last a single day.
about.sw: Mruwa ni mmea mfupi wenye matawi, wenye ugumu wa kimti kiasi, kwa kawaida kimo cha goti hadi kiuno, wenye majani yenye meno na yanayokwaruza kidogo, yaliyopangwa jozi kwa jozi kukabiliana. Maua yake huja kwenye mashada marefu membamba ya kijani yanayosimama wima kama mijeledi. Maua machache tu hufunguka kwa wakati mmoja; ni madogo, ya buluu angavu hadi zambarau, yaliyopachikwa kwenye shada, na hudumu siku moja tu.

where.en: Originally from tropical America, it is now a common weed of roadsides, compounds, farm edges and waste ground along the coast. It is also grown in gardens, and butterflies visit it constantly.
where.sw: Asili yake ni Amerika ya kitropiki, lakini sasa ni gugu la kawaida kando ya barabara, katika viwanja vya nyumba, pembezoni mwa mashamba na kwenye ardhi isiyotumika katika pwani nzima. Pia hupandwa bustanini, na vipepeo huutembelea bila kukoma.

uses.en: Pakia records it among plants valued for ornament, alongside bougainvillea, yellow oleander and lantana.
uses.sw: Pakia anaurekodi miongoni mwa mimea inayothaminiwa kama pambo, pamoja na *bougainvillea*, mharita (yellow oleander) na mvuti (lantana).

culture.en: Digo people seldom use flowers to tell plants apart; Pakia found they mostly look at leaves. The exceptions are plants whose flowers matter to people, such as perfume plants and ornamentals, and Mruwa is one of them. The name itself appears linked to the Digo word ruwa (flower) and to maruwa, the beautifying decorations Pakia describes, but Pakia does not give its meaning.
culture.sw: Wadigo mara chache hutumia maua kutofautisha mimea; Pakia aligundua kwamba mara nyingi wao huangalia majani. Isipokuwa ni mimea ambayo maua yake yana maana kwa watu, kama mimea ya manukato na ya mapambo, na Mruwa ni mmojawapo. Jina lenyewe linaonekana kuhusiana na neno la Kidigo ruwa (ua) na maruwa, mapambo ya urembo anayoyaeleza Pakia, lakini Pakia hatoi maana yake.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name Mruwa. In English it is blue porterweed or Jamaica vervain; its scientific name is Stachytarpheta jamaicensis. No Swahili name is given in the sources used here.
names.sw: Pakia anarekodi jina la Kidigo Mruwa. Kwa Kiingereza unaitwa *blue porterweed* au *Jamaica vervain*; jina lake la kisayansi ni Stachytarpheta jamaicensis. Vyanzo vilivyotumika hapa havitoi jina la Kiswahili.

reason.en: Another introduced ornamental-turned-weed in the verbena family
reason.sw: Mmea mwingine wa mapambo kutoka nje uliogeuka gugu, wa familia ya verbena

reason.en: Also identified by its ornamental flowers
reason.sw: Nao pia hutambuliwa kwa maua yake ya mapambo

reason.en: Ornamental plant recognised by its flowers
reason.sw: Mmea wa mapambo unaotambuliwa kwa maua yake
